correctness.rationale: Using a classical normal-contact quartic, the pointwise multiplicity is exactly 2+2 times the indicator of evolute interior away from a null discriminant set. Convex containment yields the internal branch; the ellipse/astroid crossing has a uniquely determined rational parameter; two actual elementary integrals yield the global formula. Thin-cap rescaling with controlled error produces the nonzero 5/2 singular coefficient and independent disk-rescaling yields the cubic far-aspect constant. All ranges, strict inequalities, and degeneracies were rederived; symbolic substitution of the crossing parameter simplifies to 1. Companion verifier passed 4439 finite checks including normal-map quadrature independent of the astroid integration. Finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The area-averaged number of Euclidean normals through a point is a longstanding Santaló-type intrinsic geometric invariant. A complete aspect-ratio classification on ellipses is a natural nontrivial exact problem. The transition is mathematically structural: a focal astroid first exits the convex ellipse at the axis-ratio threshold, creating a sharp 5/2-order loss and changing regularity, while an independent thin-endpoint boundary layer forces the cubic 4-minus-mean tail. These facts are not mere renamings, textbook pointwise classification, or an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
